reason: Good looking Victorian buttoned spoon-back ladies chair on castors in tidy re-covered condition; steady demand for these.
findings: Single photo (enlarged, legs checked). Victorian ladies' (nursing or spoon-back) chair with a deep-buttoned balloon back, low scrolled arms and a serpentine front rail, in later green cotton velvet. Four turned dark-stained legs (mahogany or walnut stain) on brass cup castors, with a swing tag on one leg. Looks like a genuine mid to late Victorian frame in sound order that has been re-covered. No maker's name, castor stamp or label visible; castors and the frame underside are not photographed in detail.
condition: Velvet is clean but flattened and faded in patches on the seat and arm fronts, with no tears seen; buttoning intact; legs polished with light scuffs; castors present on the visible legs; frame stability unknown.
rescore_note: Looks like a genuine mid to late Victorian buttoned nursing chair, re-covered in green velvet and tidy, but the frame and underside are unseen, the pile is faded in patches and a later reproduction cannot be ruled out; my judgement is the upper end of the $80 to $200 band (about $150 to $250). Estimate only, no comparable sales checked (search budget used up).
